gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the Denon PMA-600NE's optical and coaxial inputs accept only Linear PCM (32–192 kHz). Denon's manual warns that feeding it Dolby Digital, DTS or AAC from a TV 'causes noise and could damage the speakers', so the TV must be set to PCM output. The WiiM Amp Pro's HDMI ARC and optical inputs accept stereo PCM and Dolby Digital but not DTS or Atmos. The Marantz Model 50 has no digital input at all, so a TV can't connect to it directly.
standout_why: I compared against recordplayeradvice.com (Denon vs Yamaha), hifiaudiosource.com (Yamaha vs Denon), stylusandsound.com/best-stereo-amplifiers and puritybymonster.com/best-integrated-amplifiers. All four list optical and coaxial counts, and Puritybymonster says 'you need HDMI ARC or an optical input' for a TV. None says which TV audio formats those inputs accept, gives the PCM-only damage warning, or says that the Model 50 has no digital input. None gives a maker's speaker-impedance range (only power at 8 Ω and 4 Ω). None names the Denon's Bluetooth codecs: hifiaudiosource and recordplayeradvice name none, and Puritybymonster names none for the Denon. Rivals already cover the MM-only phono point: recordplayeradvice says 'neither supports a moving-coil cartridge' for the Denon and Yamaha, and stylusandsound and Puritybymonster say the WiiM Amp has no phono stage. The What Hi-Fi page returned only its headline, so I couldn't check it.
decides: This settles the 'TV and music' use case that ChatGPT offered as a filter. The WiiM Amp Pro is the only one of the four picks that takes TV sound over HDMI ARC and accepts Dolby Digital. The Denon PMA-600NE and Yamaha A-S301 use optical, and the Denon needs the TV set to PCM. The Marantz Model 50 can't take TV sound directly. For vinyl the result reverses: the Denon and Marantz have built-in MM phono stages, while the WiiM Amp Pro needs an external phono preamp.

findings.label: Digital input signal types (optical/coaxial)
findings.value: Linear PCM only, at 32, 44.1, 48, 88.2, 96, 176.4 or 192 kHz. Dolby Digital, DTS and AAC are excluded.
findings.source_title: Denon PMA-600NE Owner's Manual (NA): Connecting to a device with digital audio output connectors
findings.note: The manual says: 'Do not input non-PCM signals, such as Dolby Digital, DTS and AAC. This causes noise and could damage the speakers.' The specifications page also lists the digital interface as 'Linear PCM'.

findings.label: Speaker impedance range
findings.source_title: Denon PMA-600NE Owner's Manual (NA): Connecting speakers
findings.note: The manual says: 'Use speakers with an impedance of 4 – 16 Ω/ohms.' The specifications page repeats 'Speaker: 4 – 16 Ω'.

findings.label: Bluetooth version and codecs
findings.value: Bluetooth 5.1; SBC and AAC codecs; A2DP 1.3.2 and AVRCP 1.6.2; about 30 m (98.4 ft) line-of-sight range
findings.note: The Denon US product page lists aptX as 'No'.

findings.label: Phono input type
findings.value: MM only; 2.5 mV / 47 kΩ sensitivity, 70 mV maximum input
findings.note: The Denon US product page lists MC as 'No'.

findings.label: Price, Denon US
findings.note: Price as shown on the Denon US product page. It matches the price ChatGPT showed.

findings.label: HDMI ARC and optical input formats
findings.value: Stereo PCM and Dolby Digital. DTS and Dolby Atmos are not supported.
findings.note: The page says: 'Stereo PCM, Dolby Digital (DTS is not supported)'. It also says to 'connect to your TV's ARC/eARC-labeled port' and to set the TV to stereo PCM or Dolby Digital for HDMI ARC or optical. WiiM's FAQ says the cheaper non-Pro WiiM Amp accepts only PCM over ARC.

findings.label: Speaker impedance
findings.value: Rated for 8, 6 and 4 Ω loads, or two pairs of 8 Ω speakers in parallel; 2.67 Ω minimum
findings.note: Two pairs of 8 Ω speakers in parallel give a 4 Ω load. Power is 60 W per channel at 8 Ω and 120 W per channel at 4 Ω, per the WiiM FAQ specification table (https://faq.wiimhome.com/en/support/solutions/articles/72000616467-technical-specification-of-the-wiim-amp-and-wiim-amp-pro, modified 2025-04-30).

findings.label: Phono input
findings.value: None. Needs a turntable with a built-in preamp or an external phono preamp.
findings.note: The page says: 'No built-in phono input.' The inputs listed are HDMI ARC, optical, line and USB disk.

findings.label: Bluetooth and subwoofer output
findings.value: Bluetooth 5.3, SBC and AAC, sends and receives (A2DP sink and source). Subwoofer output with automatic cable detection and an adjustable 30–250 Hz crossover.

findings.label: Price, WiiM store
findings.note: The page text came through as '$37900', which I read as $379.00 with the decimal point dropped. ChatGPT showed $399.00. Check this before publishing.

findings.label: Digital inputs and phono type
findings.value: No digital inputs. Phono is MM only at 1.4 mV / 47 kΩ. Has a power-amp input at 1.5 V / 15 kΩ.
findings.note: The specifications page lists no optical, coaxial, USB or HDMI input. Power is 70 W x 2 at 8 Ω and 100 W x 2 at 4 Ω. Without a digital input, a TV can only connect through an external DAC or the TV's analog output.
